title: Cancer has a surprising amount of detail
author: Abhishaike Mahajan
note: Argues that cancer's biological complexity is far deeper than classical biomarkers can capture, and that the remaining unexplained patient variation demands integrating many weak signals rather than hunting for single breakthroughs. Points to ArteraAI's 2025 FDA-approved prostate cancer test as a landmark moment for black-box predictive models in oncology.

title: Pi: The Minimal Agent Within OpenClaw
author: Armin Ronacher
note: Argues that the future of coding agents lies in a minimal core (read, write, edit, bash) paired with self-extension: rather than loading pre-built plugins, the agent writes its own tools on demand. A pointed contrast to heavier orchestration frameworks and a case for embracing LLMs as code generators rather than wrapping them in elaborate scaffolding.

title: Nonlinear dynamics of multi-omics profiles during human aging
author: Xiaotao Shen et al.
note: Multi-omics profiling of 108 participants over up to 6.8 years reveals that molecular aging is not gradual but punctuated, with two pronounced waves of dysregulation at roughly ages 44 and 60. Pathways tied to oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and immune regulation shift sharply at these transitions. The authors adjusted for BMI, sex, insulin resistance, and ethnicity via linear regression residualization before analysis, though the small longitudinal cohort limits how far the cliff interpretation can be pushed.

title: nanochat
author: Andrej Karpathy
note: A minimal full-stack ChatGPT training pipeline covering tokenization, pretraining, finetuning, evaluation, and inference in a single readable codebase. Designed around one dial (transformer depth) that auto-sets all hyperparameters to produce a compute-optimal model, making a GPT-2-level chatbot trainable for under $100.

title: Time-of-day immunochemotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer: a randomized phase 3 trial
author: LungTIME-C01 investigators
note: A phase 3 trial examining whether early versus late time-of-day infusions of anti-PD-1 therapy affect outcomes in treatment-naive stage IIIC-IV NSCLC. The patient recruitment protocol, social determinants of health, and unusually smooth KM curves bring the study design into question.

title: Deep models of protein evolution in time generate realistic evolutionary trajectories and functional proteins
author: Antoine Koehl, Sebastian Prillo, Matthew Liu et al.
note: Introduces time-aware deep generative models of protein evolution that condition on phylogenetic time to produce sequences tracing realistic evolutionary trajectories. The approach moves beyond static fitness landscapes by explicitly modeling the temporal dynamics of sequence change, and the generated proteins are experimentally verified to be functional.

title: Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome
author: Žiga Avsec et al.
note: AlphaGenome still struggles most with long-range regulatory biology, where distal enhancers and complex 3D chromatin effects can sit far from the variant and remain difficult to model reliably. Its training and evaluation are also skewed toward protein-coding genes, with weaker coverage for non-coding classes (for example microRNAs) and incomplete modality coverage, since signals like DNA methylation and RNA structural features are not yet fully modeled.

title: The Adolescence of Technology
author: Dario Amodei
note: Dario's `Black seas of infinity` presents a catalogue of compounding risks, and reinforces that restraint is structurally hard because of structural incentives.

title: Some questions about biotech that I find interesting
author: Alex Telford
note: Collection of open questions about the biotech and pharma industries, spanning R&D productivity, corporate dynamics, drug discovery mechanics, and regulatory frameworks.

title: How do you use a virtual cell to do something actually useful?
author: Abhishaike Mahajan
note: Explores practical applications of virtual cell models in cancer drug development, demonstrating how computational models trained on human tumor data can identify immunotherapy responders, refine clinical trial eligibility, and discover therapeutic targets.
